strength-duos.summary: 4 rounds of 2-exercise supersets performed for 3 sets per round with controlled strength tempo.
howItWorks: Your workout is divided into 4 rounds, with 2 paired exercises (a "Duo") in each round.
In Round 1, perform Exercise A for 8–12 controlled reps, then transition to Exercise B for 8–12 reps.
Rest 45–60 seconds as needed and repeat the pair for 3 total sets before advancing to Round 2.
strength-duos.timerStructure: Self-paced sets (8–12 reps) · 3 sets per round · 4 rounds total
strength-duos.pacingTip: Choose challenging weights that bring you within 1–2 reps of fatigue by the end of each set. Focus on full range of motion rather than speed.

strength-trios.summary: 3 rounds of 3-exercise giant sets (trios) completed for 3 sets per round.
howItWorks: Your workout has 3 rounds, each containing 3 balanced exercises (mixing muscle groups so one recovers while another works).
Perform Exercise 1, Exercise 2, and Exercise 3 sequentially for 8–12 controlled reps each.
Rest 60 seconds after completing the trio, then repeat for 3 total sets before moving to the next round.
strength-trios.timerStructure: 3 exercises per round · 3 sets per round · 3 rounds total (27 working sets)
strength-trios.pacingTip: Keep transitions brisk between movements within a trio and save your main breather for the end of each set.

strength-quads.summary: 2 heavy rounds of 4 exercises: 3 sets per round structured as 2 supersets plus a double burnout finisher.
howItWorks: Each of the 2 rounds contains 4 exercises performed across 3 sets.
Pair the 4 exercises into 2 supersets (Exercises 1 & 2, and Exercises 3 & 4) for 3 sets each.
Finish the round by taking 2 of the exercises and burning out twice at the end with lighter weight or bodyweight.
strength-quads.timerStructure: 2 rounds · 4 exercises per round · 3 sets + 2x end-of-round burnout
strength-quads.pacingTip: Go heavy on the main 3 sets, then drop weight by 25–30% for the two burnout sets at the end of each round.

30-20-10-10-20-30.summary: Single-round 8-exercise HIIT pyramid where you complete all 6 timed sets (30s-20s-10s-10s-20s-30s) on one exercise before advancing.
howItWorks: You have 1 round of 8 exercises, with 6 timed interval sets performed on each exercise before moving on.
For Exercise 1, follow the reverse-pyramid clock: 30s work / 30s rest → 20s work / 20s rest → 10s work / 10s rest → 10s work / 10s rest → 20s work / 20s rest → 30s work.
Take a full 60-second recovery rest before starting the next exercise in the list of 8.
30-20-10-10-20-30.timerStructure: 8 exercises · 6 sets per exercise (30/30, 20/20, 10/10, 10/10, 20/20, 30) · 60s rest between exercises
30-20-10-10-20-30.pacingTip: The final 20s and 30s sets on the way back up the pyramid are tough because rest shrinks during the middle 10s intervals—pace your first 30s set at 85% effort.

timed-duos-40-20.summary: 4 fast-paced HIIT rounds of 2 exercises alternating 40 seconds of work with 20 seconds of rest for 3 sets.
howItWorks: Your workout has 4 rounds, with 2 exercises per round.
Start a 60-second repeating interval timer: work hard on Exercise 1 for 40 seconds, then rest and transition for 20 seconds.
Perform Exercise 2 for 40 seconds, rest 20 seconds, and repeat the duo for 3 total sets (6 minutes per round) before moving to the next round.
timed-duos-40-20.timerStructure: 40s work / 20s rest · 2 exercises × 3 sets per round · 4 rounds (24 minutes total)
timed-duos-40-20.pacingTip: With only 2 exercises alternating in a round, local muscle fatigue builds quickly. Maintain crisp form during the final 10 seconds of each 40-second interval.

timed-trios-40-20.summary: 3 HIIT rounds of 3 exercises rotating 40 seconds of work and 20 seconds of rest for 3 sets per round.
howItWorks: Your workout has 3 rounds, with 3 complementary exercises in each round.
Work for 40 seconds on Exercise 1, rest 20 seconds, work 40 seconds on Exercise 2, rest 20 seconds, work 40 seconds on Exercise 3, rest 20 seconds.
Complete 3 continuous laps of the trio (9 minutes per round) before advancing to the next round.
timed-trios-40-20.timerStructure: 40s work / 20s rest · 3 exercises × 3 sets per round · 3 rounds (27 minutes total)
timed-trios-40-20.pacingTip: Use the 20-second window to get set up for the next movement so you can start moving the instant the 40-second work bell rings.

8-excercises-40-20.summary: Full-circuit HIIT: 1 big list of 8 exercises performed for 40s work / 20s rest, repeated for 3 full circuits.
howItWorks: All 8 generated exercises form a single continuous station circuit.
Perform each exercise for 40 seconds of work followed by 20 seconds of rest/transition down the list from Exercise 1 to Exercise 8 (8 minutes per lap).
Complete 3 full laps of the 8-exercise circuit for a 24-minute total conditioning session.
8-excercises-40-20.timerStructure: 40s work / 20s rest · 8 exercises per circuit · 3 circuits total (24 sets)
8-excercises-40-20.pacingTip: Because you only revisit each exercise once every 8 minutes, you can push higher intensity on every 40-second interval.

10-to-1-to-10.summary: Rep-ladder conditioning: 5 exercises performed from 10 reps down to 1 rep and back up to 10 reps (20 sets total).
howItWorks: Cycle through all 5 generated exercises continuously on a rep ladder.
Lap 1: Perform 10 reps of each of the 5 exercises (per side for unilateral movements). Lap 2: 9 reps of each, continuing down to 1 rep of each on Lap 10.
Then climb back up the ladder from 1 rep back to 10 reps (20 total laps / 110 total reps per exercise).
10-to-1-to-10.pacingTip: Treat the middle sets (5 down to 1 and 1 up to 5) as active recovery with smooth transitions so you have energy for the sets of 8, 9, and 10 at the end.

6-excercise-pyramid.summary: Add-on / drop-off timed pyramid across 6 exercises over 11 progressive rounds (30s per exercise, 10s transition between exercises, 60s rest at end of set).
howItWorks: Set 1: Do 30s of Exercise 1, then rest 60s. Set 2: Do 30s of Ex 1 → 10s Transition → 30s of Ex 2, then rest 60s.
Keep adding one exercise each set (with a 10s transition between exercises) until Set 6, where you perform all 6 exercises for 30s each, then rest 60s.
On Sets 7–11, drop Exercise 1, then Exercise 2, etc., until Set 11 finishes with 30s of Exercise 6 followed by a 60s rest.
6-excercise-pyramid.timerStructure: 6 exercises · 11 pyramid sets (30s work / 10s transition between exercises / 60s rest per set)
6-excercise-pyramid.pacingTip: You will perform every exercise 6 times over the pyramid. Use the 10-second transition timer to move briskly to the next station and save your full breather for the 60-second rest at the end of each set.

8x8-duos.summary: 4 AMRAP rounds of 2 exercises: alternate 8 reps of each exercise non-stop for 8 minutes per round.
howItWorks: Your workout has 4 rounds, each pairing 2 exercises together.
Set an 8-minute countdown clock for Round 1. Perform 8 reps of Exercise A, immediately switch to 8 reps of Exercise B, and repeat back-and-forth with no scheduled rest.
Log as many quality rounds as possible in 8 minutes, rest 60–90 seconds, and begin the next 8-minute Duo.
8x8-duos.timerStructure: 4 rounds · 8-minute AMRAP per round · 8 reps Exercise A ↔ 8 reps Exercise B
8x8-duos.pacingTip: 8 minutes of continuous work is an aerobic test—pick a sustainable rhythm from minute 1 rather than sprinting out of the gate.

5-constant-5-change-40-20.summary: 3 rounds alternating a round-specific "Constant" exercise (first 3 generated exercises) with 5 shared "Changing" exercises at 40s/20s.
howItWorks: Of your 8 generated exercises, Exercises 1, 2, and 3 are your Round Constants (one per round), and Exercises 4–8 are your 5 shared Changing exercises.
In Round 1 (10 sets at 40s work / 20s rest): alternate Constant #1 (Exercise 1) with each of the 5 Changing exercises (Ex 1 → Ex 4 → Ex 1 → Ex 5 → Ex 1 → Ex 6 → Ex 1 → Ex 7 → Ex 1 → Ex 8).
Repeat the same 10-set alternating structure in Round 2 using Constant #2 (Exercise 2) and in Round 3 using Constant #3 (Exercise 3).
5-constant-5-change-40-20.timerStructure: 3 rounds · 10 sets per round (40s/20s) · Constant exercise repeated 5x per round
5-constant-5-change-40-20.pacingTip: You will perform each Constant exercise 5 times inside its round! Pace yourself on the Constant slots and use the Changing slots to shift load to other muscle groups.

push-ups.summary: Classic bodyweight horizontal press targeting the chest, anterior shoulders, triceps, and core.
steps: Start in a rigid high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, wrists stacked under elbows, and glutes braced.
Lower your chest toward the floor in a straight line while keeping elbows angled roughly 45° from your torso.
Press forcefully through your palms back to full arm extension without letting your hips sag or hike.
push-ups.formTip: Screw your palms outward into the floor to engage your lats and protect your shoulder joints.

3-stop-pushups.summary: Tempo push-up variation featuring 3 distinct isometric pause stops per repetition to maximize chest and tricep time-under-tension.
steps: From a high plank, lower halfway down (Stop 1) and hold for 1 full second.
Lower to 1 inch above the floor (Stop 2) and hold for 1 full second with chest hovering.
Press halfway back up (Stop 3) and hold for 1 second before locking out at the top.
3-stop-pushups.formTip: Keep your core tight during all three pause points so your lower back never arches when fatigue sets in.

pushups-with-shoulder-tap.summary: Anti-rotation push-up combining a full chest press with alternating single-arm shoulder taps at the top of each rep.
steps: Set up in a high plank with feet slightly wider than hip-width for a stable base.
Perform a full push-up and return to the top plank position.
Brace your abs and glutes to keep your hips completely level as you lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, then alternate.
pushups-with-shoulder-tap.formTip: Pretend a cup of water is resting on your lower back—resist any side-to-side hip sway during the tap.

chest-flys.summary: Wide-arc dumbbell chest isolation exercise stretching and contracting the pectoral fibers.
steps: Lie flat on a bench or floor holding dumbbells directly above your chest with palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Open your arms wide in a smooth arc until your elbows reach chest level and you feel a deep stretch across your pecs.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together along the same arc, maintaining the fixed slight elbow bend.
chest-flys.formTip: Think about hugging a wide tree barrel—do not turn the movement into a bent-arm press.

chest-press-6-6-6.summary: 18-rep dumbbell chest press complex: 6 bilateral reps, 6 right-arm reps with left held isometric, and 6 left-arm reps with right held isometric.
steps: Lie on a bench or floor pressing both dumbbells together for 6 full bilateral repetitions, finishing with both weights held at the top.
Keep the left dumbbell locked out overhead while performing 6 single-arm presses with the right arm.
Keep the right dumbbell locked out overhead while performing 6 single-arm presses with the left arm (18 total reps).
chest-press-6-6-6.formTip: Actively press the stationary dumbbell toward the ceiling during the single-arm sets to maintain upper-chest tension.

trx-chest-press.summary: Suspended incline push-up on TRX straps challenging chest pressing strength alongside deep shoulder and core stability.
steps: Stand facing away from the TRX anchor holding the handles at chest height with straps taut and body in a straight incline plank.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest between your hands while keeping the straps lightly grazing above your forearms.
Press your palms together and away to return to the starting incline plank without letting the straps saw against your arms.
trx-chest-press.formTip: Walk your feet closer to the anchor point to increase the incline and make the press heavier.

up-up-down-ups.summary: Dynamic plank-to-pushup (commando plank) transitioning between forearms and hands, with optional lateral hand/foot taps.
steps: Begin in a forearm plank with elbows directly beneath your shoulders and core braced.
Place one palm flat under your shoulder and press up, followed by the other palm to reach a high plank ("Up-Up").
Optionally perform a lateral hand/foot tap at the top, then lower back down one forearm at a time ("Down-Down"), alternating your lead arm every rep.
up-up-down-ups.formTip: Place your hand exactly where your elbow just was so you press straight up with your triceps and chest.

curls.summary: Elbow flexion exercise using dumbbells, resistance bands, or TRX straps to isolate and build the biceps.
steps: Stand tall (or lean back on TRX straps) with elbows pinned close to your ribcage and palms facing forward.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders by contracting your biceps while keeping your upper arms completely stationary.
Pause and squeeze at peak contraction before lowering slowly under control to full elbow extension.
curls.formTip: Avoid swinging your torso or letting your elbows drift forward—make the biceps move 100% of the load.

skull-crushers.summary: Supine lying tricep extension isolating all three heads of the triceps.
steps: Lie on your back on a bench or mat holding dumbbells or a weight straight above your shoulders with palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms vertical and stationary as you hinge only at the elbows, lowering the weights toward your temples/forehead.
Extend your forearms straight back up using your triceps to lock out at the top.
skull-crushers.formTip: Angle your upper arms slightly back (about 10° toward your head) to keep constant tension on the triceps even at the top.

tricep-kick-backs.summary: Bent-over dumbbell tricep extension targeting peak contraction of the triceps.
steps: Hinge forward at the hips to a 45°–60° torso angle with a flat back, tucking your upper arms parallel to your torso.
Keeping your elbows glued to your sides, extend your forearms straight back until your arms are fully locked out behind you.
Squeeze the triceps for a half-second at the top, then lower the dumbbells back to a 90° elbow bend.
tricep-kick-backs.formTip: Never let your elbows drop during the set—only your forearm should move like a pendulum.

trx-triceps.summary: Suspended bodyweight overhead tricep extension on TRX straps.
steps: Stand facing away from the TRX anchor in a forward incline plank with arms extended forward at forehead height and palms facing down.
Keep your elbows pointed straight ahead and shoulder-width apart as you bend at the elbows, lowering your forehead behind your hands.
Press through your palms to extend your elbows back to the starting position while holding a rigid body line.
trx-triceps.formTip: Keep your elbows tucked in rather than flaring wide so all the torque stays on your triceps.

chair-dips.summary: Bodyweight bench or chair dip targeting the triceps, anterior deltoids, and lower chest.
steps: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair or bench, gripping the front edge next to your hips with fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips just off the front edge (knees bent for standard or legs straight for advanced) and lower until elbows reach 90°.
Press through the heels of your palms to straighten your arms back to the top.
chair-dips.formTip: Keep your back grazing close to the front edge of the chair—drifting forward shifts stress onto the front of the shoulder.

shoulder-press.summary: Vertical overhead press using dumbbells or resistance bands to build deltoid and tricep strength.
steps: Stand or sit tall holding dumbbells or band handles at shoulder height with palms facing forward or neutral.
Brace your core and glutes, then press the weights straight overhead until your arms are fully extended by your ears.
Lower slowly back to shoulder level with control before beginning the next rep.
shoulder-press.formTip: Keep your ribs tucked down so you press strictly with your shoulders rather than leaning back into an incline press.

arnold-press.summary: Rotational dumbbell shoulder press hitting the anterior, lateral, and posterior deltoids through a 180° pronation arc.
steps: Start with dumbbells held in front of your chin with palms facing toward you (like the top of a bicep curl).
In one fluid motion, open your elbows out to the sides while rotating your palms forward and pressing the dumbbells overhead.
Reverse the motion on the way down, rotating your palms back toward your face as the weights return to chin height.
arnold-press.formTip: Keep the rotation smooth and continuous throughout the press rather than breaking it into two robotic steps.

lateral-shoulder-raises.summary: Abduction raise with dumbbells or bands isolating the lateral (medial) head of the deltoids.
steps: Stand tall holding dumbbells or a resistance band at your sides with a soft 10° bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until your elbows reach shoulder height (forming a "T").
Pause briefly at shoulder level, then lower slowly for 2–3 seconds to resist gravity.
lateral-shoulder-raises.formTip: Lead with your elbows rather than your wrists, and keep your shoulders relaxed down away from your ears.

cheerleaders.summary: Multi-angle shoulder raise complex combining front, diagonal ("V"), and lateral raises with light dumbbells.
steps: Stand tall with light-to-moderate dumbbells at your thighs and a braced core.
Raise both arms straight in front to shoulder height, lower, then raise diagonally into a high "V" (cheerleader stance).
Lower with control and finish the sequence with a lateral raise out to a "T", repeating the multi-angle pattern rhythmically.
cheerleaders.formTip: Use lighter weights than your standard shoulder press—the long lever arm creates intense deltoid burn quickly.

swings.summary: Explosive hip-hinge kettlebell or dumbbell swing driving power from the glutes, hamstrings, and back.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, holding a kettlebell or dumbbell with both hands between your thighs.
Hinge your hips back sharply with a flat back (shins nearly vertical) to load your hamstrings and glutes.
Snap your hips forward explosively to float the weight up to chest/shoulder height, then let it swing back between your hips for the next rep.
swings.formTip: A swing is a horizontal hip snap, not a squat—your arms act like ropes while your glutes generate 100% of the upward drive.

trx-i-y-ts.summary: Three-angle TRX suspension rear-delt and upper-back fly sequence forming the letters "I", "Y", and "T".
steps: Lean back holding the TRX handles with arms extended in front of you and body in a straight plank.
Pull your body up by raising straight arms overhead into an "I", lower with control, then pull up at a 45° angle into a "Y".
Lower again, then pull your arms straight out to the sides into a "T" by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
trx-i-y-ts.formTip: Keep your elbows straight and hips locked in line with your torso—never break at the waist to pull yourself up.

trx-wood-choppers.summary: Rotational TRX core and upper-back torso sweep targeting the obliques, abs, lats, and shoulders.
steps: Stand sideways to the TRX anchor holding both handles together with interlocked hands and arms extended.
Lean away with a rigid torso, then drive through your core and back to rotate your arms diagonally across and up like chopping wood.
Return slowly under rotational control and complete all reps or half the interval on one side before switching.
trx-wood-choppers.formTip: Initiate the rotation from your ribcage and obliques while keeping your arms long and shoulders packed.

rows.summary: Horizontal pulling movement using dumbbells, bands, or TRX to strengthen the lats, rhomboids, rear delts, and biceps.
steps: Hinge forward 45° with a flat back (for dumbbells/bands) or lean back on TRX straps with arms extended.
Drive your elbows back past your ribcage while squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the pull.
Lower the weights or extend your arms slowly back to a full stretch without rounding your upper back.
rows.formTip: Think about pulling with your elbows toward your back pockets rather than curling with your wrists.

pull-ups.summary: Overhand-grip vertical pull targeting the latissimus dorsi, upper back, biceps, and core.
steps: Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away from you (pronated grip).
Depress your shoulder blades down and back, then pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down to your sides.
Once your chin clears the bar, lower yourself smoothly all the way to a controlled dead hang.
pull-ups.formTip: Cross your ankles or hollow your core slightly to prevent swinging and keep strict tension on your lats.

chin-ups.summary: Underhand-grip vertical pull placing heavy emphasis on both the biceps and latissimus dorsi.
steps: Grip the bar at shoulder-width with palms facing toward you (supinated grip).
Pull yourself upward by drawing your elbows down in front of your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Squeeze your biceps and lats at the top, then lower under full control to straight arms.
chin-ups.formTip: Lead with your chest toward the bar and keep your shoulders rolled back at the top.

face-pulls.summary: Banded high row with external shoulder rotation targeting the rear deltoids, rhomboids, and rotator cuff.
steps: Anchor a resistance band at upper-chest or eye level and hold the ends with both hands, stepping back to create tension.
Pull the band toward your forehead while driving your elbows high and wide and rotating your thumbs back behind your ears.
Pause for 1 second in a "double bicep" pose squeezing your upper back, then return slowly.
face-pulls.formTip: Your hands should finish by your ears, not your chest—external rotation at the end is what fires the rotator cuff.

reverse-flys.summary: Bent-over rear deltoid and upper-back dumbbell fly strengthening postural scapular retractors.
steps: Hinge at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, holding dumbbells beneath your chest with palms facing each other.
Maintaining a slight bend in your elbows, sweep your arms out wide toward the ceiling until they are in line with your back.
Squeeze your rear delts and mid-back at the top, then lower slowly without swinging your torso.
reverse-flys.formTip: Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor a few feet ahead rather than cranking your head up.

serratus-pushups.summary: Straight-arm scapular push-up isolating the serratus anterior and shoulder girdle stabilizers.
steps: Assume a rigid high plank with arms locked straight and hands stacked directly beneath your shoulders.
Keeping your elbows 100% straight, let your chest sink slightly so your shoulder blades pinch together.
Push the floor away forcefully to spread your shoulder blades wide apart and dome your upper back slightly at the top.
serratus-pushups.formTip: Zero elbow bend—all the movement happens in a 2–3 inch range at the shoulder blades.

slam-ball-slams.summary: Explosive full-body overhead slam using a non-bounce slam ball to train the lats, abs, shoulders, and hip hinge.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a slam ball at hip level.
Reach the ball high overhead into full triple extension (hips, knees, and ankles extended) while inhaling.
Brace your abs and lats to violently slam the ball straight down between your feet while hinging into an athletic squat to catch it.
slam-ball-slams.formTip: Drop your hips down with the ball as you slam so you pick it up with a flat back and loaded legs, not a rounded spine.

ab-wheel-roller.summary: High-tension anti-extension core rollout using an ab wheel or foam roller to challenge the abs, lats, and shoulders.
steps: Kneel on a mat gripping the ab wheel handles directly beneath your shoulders, tucking your pelvis slightly into a posterior tilt.
Roll the wheel forward slowly while keeping your abs braced tight and hips moving forward as one unit with your torso.
Roll out as far as you can without letting your lower back arch, then contract your abs and lats to pull the wheel back under your shoulders.
ab-wheel-roller.formTip: Never let your lower back sag—keep a slight hollow-body rib tuck throughout the entire rollout.

trx-crunches.summary: Suspended plank knee-tuck (or straight-leg pike) with feet hooked in TRX straps.
steps: Hook both feet into the low TRX foot cradles and press up into a solid high plank with wrists under shoulders.
For a TRX Crunch, drive both knees in toward your chest while rounding your lower abs; for a Pike, keep legs straight and lift your hips high toward the ceiling.
Extend your legs smoothly back to a neutral plank without letting your hips drop below shoulder level.
trx-crunches.formTip: Pause for a half-second when your knees are tucked or hips are piked to eliminate pendulum momentum.

leg-lifts.summary: Supine straight-leg raise targeting the lower rectus abdominis and hip flexors.
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs straight together and hands resting at your sides or tucked lightly beneath your outer hips.
Press your lower back firmly into the mat and lift both straight legs up to a 90° vertical angle.
Lower your legs slowly toward the floor (stopping 2 inches above the ground) while keeping your lower back glued down.
leg-lifts.formTip: If your lower back starts lifting off the mat near the bottom, bend your knees slightly or limit the bottom range.

3-way-v-ups.summary: Tri-directional V-up series folding to the left, center, and right to hit the upper/lower abs and both obliques.
steps: Lie flat on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight out.
Fold your torso and legs up together into a "V", reaching both hands outside your left foot (1), then lower back down.
Fold straight up the center reaching toward your toes (2), lower, then fold up reaching outside your right foot (3).
3-way-v-ups.formTip: Exhale sharply as you fold up on each of the three angles to maximize abdominal contraction.

v-ups-with-the-ball.summary: Weighted V-up passing or reaching a slam ball/medicine ball between hands and feet at the peak of the fold.
steps: Lie extended on your back holding a slam ball or weight with both hands overhead.
Simultaneously lift your torso and straight legs into a "V" position, bringing the ball up to meet your shins/toes.
Lower your arms and legs back toward the floor under tight abdominal control without resting completely between reps.
v-ups-with-the-ball.formTip: Keep your chin slightly tucked and lift your entire shoulder blades off the mat on every rep.

crunches.summary: Focused upper abdominal spinal flexion movement isolating the rectus abdominis.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent at 90°, feet flat on the floor, and fingertips lightly behind your ears.
Exhale and curl your upper spine to lift your head and shoulder blades off the mat while pressing your lower back down.
Hold the top squeeze for 1 second, then lower slowly back to the mat.
crunches.formTip: Never pull on your neck with your hands—keep a fist-sized space between your chin and chest.

bicycle-crunches.summary: Alternating rotational crunch pairing opposite elbow-to-knee touches with pedaling leg extensions.
steps: Lie on your back with knees lifted to tabletop, shoulders curled off the mat, and hands lightly behind your head.
Extend your right leg straight out at a 45° angle while rotating your right armpit/elbow across to meet your left knee.
Switch sides smoothly in a pedaling motion, bringing your left elbow to your right knee while fully extending the left leg.
bicycle-crunches.formTip: Rotate your entire shoulder and ribcage toward the knee rather than just flapping your elbows inward.

mountain-climbers.summary: High-tempo plank knee drives combining core stabilization with cardiovascular conditioning.
steps: Start in a strong high plank with hands stacked directly under shoulders and body in a straight line.
Drive one knee rapidly toward your chest while keeping your hips low and back flat.
Switch legs rhythmically in a running plank motion while pressing the floor away through your palms.
mountain-climbers.formTip: Keep your shoulders stacked directly over your wrists—do not let yourself drift backward into a downward dog.

plank.summary: Isometric full-body core hold building endurance in the transverse abdominis, rectus abdominis, shoulders, and glutes.
steps: Set your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders and legs extended behind you.
Tuck your tailbone slightly, squeeze your quads and glutes, and brace your abs as if preparing for a punch.
Hold a completely straight line from head to heels while breathing steadily.
plank.formTip: Pull your elbows isometrically toward your toes to double the activation in your abs.

plank-jacks.summary: Dynamic plank jumping both feet wide and together to challenge anti-extension core stability and hip abductors.
steps: Begin in a high plank or forearm plank with feet together and core tightly braced.
Hop both feet out wide (wider than shoulder-width) like a horizontal jumping jack while keeping your hips level.
Immediately hop your feet back together without letting your lower back bounce or dip.
plank-jacks.formTip: Land softly on the balls of your feet and keep your hips at the exact same height throughout.

round-the-worlds-plank-raises.summary: Four-point anti-rotation plank sequentially raising your left arm, right arm, right leg, and left leg around the clock.
steps: Set up in a high or forearm plank with feet slightly wider than hip-width for rotational balance.
Without shifting your hips, reach your left arm straight forward for 1 count, then set it down; reach your right arm forward, then set it down.
Lift your right leg straight up squeezing the glute, set it down, then lift your left leg straight up to complete one full lap "around the world".
round-the-worlds-plank-raises.formTip: Move deliberately around the 4 limbs—rushing causes your torso to twist.

opposite-arm-and-leg-lifts.summary: Contralateral quadruped (bird-dog) or prone extension strengthening the spinal erectors, abs, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips (or lying prone on the mat).
Brace your core and simultaneously extend your right arm straight forward and your left leg straight back until both are parallel to the floor.
Pause for 1 second reaching long from fingertips to heel, return to start, and switch to left arm and right leg.
opposite-arm-and-leg-lifts.formTip: Think about reaching long horizontally rather than kicking high, which prevents overarching your lower back.

side-plank-with-hip-dip.summary: Lateral core, oblique, and glute medius exercise lowering and lifting the hips from a forearm side plank (with optional top-leg abduction raise at the top).
steps: Lie on your side propped on one forearm with your elbow stacked directly beneath your shoulder and feet stacked.
Lift your hips into a straight side plank line, then slowly lower your bottom hip down until it lightly hovers above the mat.
Contract your bottom oblique and glute medius to drive your hips back up—optionally lifting your top leg at the peak for added glute medius load.
side-plank-with-hip-dip.formTip: Keep your chest and hips facing straight forward as if sliding between two panes of glass.

side-plank-with-reach-under.summary: Rotational side plank threading the top arm underneath the ribcage and extending back up to target the obliques.
steps: Start in a forearm or high side plank with your top arm extended straight toward the ceiling.
Keeping your hips elevated, rotate your torso to thread your top arm underneath your lower ribcage.
Unwind smoothly and open your chest back out, reaching your top hand straight back up to the ceiling.
side-plank-with-reach-under.formTip: Follow your moving hand with your eyes to encourage full thoracic spine rotation.

russian-twists-with-slam-ball.summary: Seated V-sit rotational core exercise tapping a slam ball or weight side-to-side across the hips.
steps: Sit on the mat with knees bent, leaning your torso back 45° with a tall spine (heels lightly down or lifted off the floor) holding a slam ball.
Rotate your shoulders and ribcage to bring the slam ball beside your right hip.
Brace your obliques to sweep the ball across your torso to your left hip in a controlled rhythm.
russian-twists-with-slam-ball.formTip: Turn your shoulders with the ball—if only your arms move side-to-side while your chest faces forward, your obliques do less work.

single-leg-leg-lifts-on-bench-with-weigh.summary: Weighted unilateral hip extension / leg lift performed on a bench to isolate the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Position yourself on a bench (either supine in a single-leg hip thrust setup with weight on your hip crease, or prone/side-supported with weight at the working leg/hip).
Brace your core and drive through your working leg/glute to lift and extend the hip to full lockout.
Pause for 1 full second squeezing the glute at the top before lowering under control; switch legs halfway.
single-leg-leg-lifts-on-bench-with-weigh.formTip: Keep your chin tucked and ribs down at the top of the lift so all extension comes from the hip joint, not the lower spine.

single-leg-band-glute-bridge.summary: Unilateral supine glute bridge with a resistance band above the knees to fire the glute maximus, glute medius, and hamstrings.
steps: Lie on your back with a loop band just above your knees, one foot planted near your glutes and the other leg extended or held at 90°.
Press through the heel of your planted foot while keeping tension outward against the band to lift your hips into a straight bridge.
Squeeze your working glute at the top for 1 second, lower slowly, and switch legs halfway through the set.
single-leg-band-glute-bridge.formTip: Keep both hip bones level with the ceiling—do not let the unweighted hip drop.

alternating-glute-bridge-and-butterflies.summary: Banded supine glute bridge holding at the top to perform a knees-out butterfly abduction on every rep.
steps: Lie on your back with a resistance band looped above your knees and feet planted hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a high glute bridge.
While holding your hips at the top, press both knees outward against the band ("butterfly"), bring knees back to neutral, then lower your hips down.
alternating-glute-bridge-and-butterflies.formTip: Keep your hips fully elevated during the butterfly abduction—do not let your glutes sink while pushing the knees out.

lateral-band-walks.summary: Athletic side-to-side lateral steps and forward/backward monster walks in a low quarter-squat with a hip or ankle resistance band.
steps: Place a loop band around your ankles or just above your knees and sink into an athletic quarter-squat with chest up.
Take wide lateral steps to the right while keeping toes pointed straight ahead, then reverse to the left without letting your feet touch.
Optionally alternate with 4–6 diagonal forward and backward "Monster Walk" steps while maintaining low hip height.
lateral-band-walks.formTip: Never let your feet come all the way together—keep at least hip-width tension on the band at all times.

band-leg-kick-backs-and-diagonals.summary: Standing banded hip extension alternating straight-back kickbacks with 45° diagonal glute kickbacks.
steps: Loop a resistance band around your ankles and stand tall (optionally lightly touching a wall or chair for balance).
Keeping your working leg straight and core braced, kick one heel straight back squeezing the glute maximus.
Return with control, then kick the same leg back at a 45° diagonal angle to hit the upper/outer glute medius; switch legs halfway.
band-leg-kick-backs-and-diagonals.formTip: Keep your torso upright—leaning forward turns a glute kickback into a lower-back tilt.

frog-pumps.summary: High-rep supine glute bridge with the soles of your feet pressed together and knees butterflied open.
steps: Lie on your back, press the soles of your shoes together (like a frog or butterfly stretch), and pull your heels close to your glutes.
Tuck your chin slightly and drive through the outer edges of your feet to bridge your hips up.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and pump rhythmically while keeping your knees flared wide.
frog-pumps.formTip: Tucking your chin and looking toward your knees helps lock your ribcage down for a stronger glute contraction.

squats.summary: Foundational lower-body squat (Olympic barbell back/front squat from rack, goblet squat, or bodyweight) building quad, glute, and core strength.
steps: Unrack a barbell across your upper traps/front delts (or hold a 35–50 lb dumbbell goblet-style) with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out 10°–15°.
Sit your hips back and down while tracking your knees outward in line with your toes until thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your mid-foot and heels to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
squats.formTip: Keep your chest proud and full foot anchored—never let your knees cave inward on the ascent.

sumo-squats.summary: Wide-stance squat with toes turned out 45° emphasizing the glutes, inner thighs (adductors), and quads.
steps: Take a wide stance (well outside shoulder-width) and turn your toes out at a 45° angle.
Keep your torso upright as you lower your hips straight down while actively pressing your knees outward toward your pinky toes.
Drive through your heels to return to standing, squeezing your glutes and inner thighs at the top.
sumo-squats.formTip: Because of the wide stance, keep your torso more vertical than a standard squat.

1-5-squats.summary: One-and-a-half rep pulse & isometric hold squat: descend to the bottom, rise halfway up, pause/drop back to the bottom, and stand all the way up.
steps: Lower into a full-depth parallel squat (with barbell, goblet dumbbell, or bodyweight) and hold active bottom tension.
Press halfway up (about 45° knee angle), pause for 1 full second, then lower all the way back down into the bottom of the squat.
Drive forcefully from the bottom all the way to standing—that entire sequence counts as 1 rep!
1-5-squats.formTip: Control the isometric pause at the bottom and halfway point rather than bouncing out of the hole.

wide-then-narrow-squats.summary: Dynamic squat variation alternating between a wide sumo stance and a narrow shoulder-width stance.
steps: Perform a full squat in a wide stance with knees tracking outward.
As you stand or hop lightly at the top, step or hop your feet inward to a narrow hip-width stance and immediately squat down.
Continue alternating 1 Wide Squat and 1 Narrow Squat rhythmically.
wide-then-narrow-squats.formTip: Wide squats emphasize glutes and inner thighs; narrow squats shift emphasis directly onto the outer quads.

squat-jumps.summary: Plyometric vertical jump squat developing lower-body explosive power and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a quarter-to-parallel squat while swinging your arms back.
Drive explosively through the floor, extending hips, knees, and ankles to launch vertically into the air.
Land softly toe-to-heel with bent knees, absorbing the impact smoothly into the next squat.
squat-jumps.formTip: Aim for quiet, athletic landings—soft landings protect your knees and load your muscles properly.

step-ups.summary: Unilateral bench or box step-up driving through the lead heel to build quad and glute strength.
steps: Place one entire foot flat on top of a sturdy bench, box, or step (bodyweight or holding dumbbells).
Lean your torso slightly forward over your front knee and drive through your elevated heel to stand all the way up on the bench.
Lower yourself back down slowly over 2 seconds using the elevated leg before switching or repeating.
step-ups.formTip: Avoid pushing off the floor with your back toes—make the top leg lift 100% of your bodyweight.

lunges-split-squats.summary: Unilateral split-squat or stepping lunge targeting the quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
steps: Step into a split stance with feet hip-width apart laterally (like standing on train tracks, not a tightrope).
Lower your back knee toward the floor until both front and back knees form 90° angles.
Drive through your front heel and mid-foot to return to standing; alternate legs or split the interval evenly.
lunges-split-squats.formTip: Keep your front shin nearly vertical and torso tall to share the load evenly between quads and glutes.

lunge-jumps.summary: Plyometric split-squat jump switching lead legs mid-air for high-intensity leg power.
steps: Start at the bottom of a split lunge with both knees bent at 90° and torso upright.
Drive explosively through both feet to jump straight up and scissor-switch your legs in mid-air.
Land softly in a lunge on the opposite leg, absorbing the impact immediately into the next jump.
lunge-jumps.formTip: Use a rhythmic opposing arm swing (like sprinting) to help generate lift and balance.

lunges-with-one-dumbbell-up.summary: Unilateral lunge holding a single dumbbell locked out overhead to challenge glutes, quads, shoulder stability, and core.
steps: Press one dumbbell straight overhead with your bicep locked by your ear and wrist neutral.
Keeping the weight stacked directly over your shoulder, step into a controlled lunge until both knees hit 90°.
Drive through your front heel back to standing; switch the overhead arm halfway through the set.
lunges-with-one-dumbbell-up.formTip: Keep your elbow locked straight overhead—looking at a fixed spot ahead helps maintain balance.

lunge-with-one-foot-on-bench.summary: Rear-foot-elevated split squat (Bulgarian split squat) placing deep stretch and load on the front glute and quad.
steps: Stand about two feet in front of a bench and rest the laces of your back foot on top of the bench.
Lower your hips down and slightly back until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive powerfully through your front heel to stand tall; complete half the set on each leg.
lunge-with-one-foot-on-bench.formTip: Hinging your torso forward 15° increases glute recruitment; staying vertical emphasizes the quad.

lunge-twists-with-slam-ball.summary: Stepping lunge combined with a torso rotation over the front leg while holding a slam ball.
steps: Hold a slam ball at chest height with elbows wide and step forward or backward into a 90° lunge.
At the bottom of the lunge, rotate your torso and the slam ball across toward your front knee/hip.
Return to center and drive through your front heel back to standing, alternating legs.
lunge-twists-with-slam-ball.formTip: Always twist toward the side of your front leg—this locks the pelvis in place and isolates the obliques.

bear-crawls.summary: Quadruped knees-hovering crawl building shoulder stability, core anti-rotation, and quad endurance.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders, knees under hips, and lift your knees just 1–2 inches off the floor.
Crawl forward by moving your opposite hand and foot simultaneously (right hand + left foot, then left hand + right foot) in short steps.
Crawl forward several steps, then crawl backward for the same distance while keeping your back flat and knees low.
bear-crawls.formTip: Take small 6-inch steps and keep your knees hovering right above the floor—do not let your hips rise up high.

burpees.summary: Full-body metabolic conditioning exercise combining a squat thrust, plank/push-up, and vertical jump.
steps: From standing, squat down and place both hands flat on the floor in front of your feet.
Hop or step both feet back into a tight high plank (optionally dropping your chest to the floor for a push-up).
Snap both feet back in wide outside your hands and explode straight up into a vertical jump with hands reaching overhead.
burpees.formTip: Snap your feet back in flat-footed rather than landing on your toes—this protects your knees and sets up an easy jump.

single-leg-deadlift.summary: Unilateral hip-hinge balance exercise targeting the hamstrings, glutes, lower back, and ankle/core stabilizers.
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft 15° knee bend, holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hip by extending your free leg straight back behind you like a seesaw while lowering the weights along your standing shin.
When your torso and back leg reach parallel to the floor, drive your standing hip forward by squeezing your glute and hamstring to stand tall.
single-leg-deadlift.formTip: Point the toes of your lifted back foot straight down toward the floor to keep your hips square.

trx-hamstring-curls.summary: Supine hamstring curl with heels suspended in TRX straps, intensely working the hamstrings, glutes, and core.
steps: Lie on your back facing the TRX anchor and place both heels into the low TRX foot cradles.
Press your hips off the mat to form a straight supine plank from shoulders to heels.
Dig your heels down and curl them in toward your glutes while lifting your hips higher, then extend slowly back out.
trx-hamstring-curls.formTip: Keep your hips elevated during both the curl in and the extension out to prevent hamstring cramping and maximize glute synergy.

incline-barbell-bench-press.summary: Heavy upper-chest compound press using an Olympic barbell on a 30°–45° incline bench to build clavicular pectoral, anterior deltoid, and tricep mass.
steps: Set your adjustable bench to a 30°–45° incline inside the squat rack and grip the Olympic barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar over your upper chest and lower it under control until it lightly touches your upper sternum just below the collarbones.
Drive your feet into the floor and press the barbell straight up and slightly back to full lockout.
incline-barbell-bench-press.formTip: Keep your elbows tucked at roughly a 45°–60° angle to your torso rather than flaring 90° out to protect your shoulders and maximize upper-pec drive.

barbell-bench-press.summary: Primary horizontal barbell press from the squat rack & flat bench to overload the pectorals, triceps, and anterior deltoids beyond 50 lb dumbbell limits.
steps: Lie flat on the bench under your rack with eyes beneath the Olympic barbell, feet planted firmly, and shoulder blades pinched together.
Unrack the bar with straight arms, then lower it in a controlled arc to your mid-chest/sternum.
Press the bar forcefully back up over your shoulders while keeping your glutes and upper back anchored to the bench.
barbell-bench-press.formTip: Maintain a slight natural arch in your mid-back with your shoulder blades retracted down into the bench pad throughout every rep.

landmine-single-arm-press.summary: Angled unilateral shoulder press using the landmine attachment to build deltoid, upper-chest, tricep, and anti-rotation core strength in a shoulder-friendly arc.
steps: Stand in a staggered split stance or half-kneeling position holding the loaded end of the landmine barbell at shoulder height in one hand.
Brace your abs and glutes, then press the barbell sleeve up and forward along its natural diagonal arc to full lockout.
Lean your torso slightly into the top of the press so your bicep finishes by your ear, then lower slowly back to your shoulder; switch arms after completing your reps.
landmine-single-arm-press.formTip: Keep your ribcage stacked over your pelvis—do not let the asymmetric load twist your shoulders or arch your lower back.

barbell-push-press.summary: Explosive overhead barbell press using a crisp quarter-squat leg drive to launch heavy barbell loads overhead for total-body power and shoulder strength.
steps: Unrack the Olympic barbell in a front-rack position resting across your front deltoids/clavicles with elbows slightly forward and feet hip-width apart.
Dip your knees 3–4 inches into a brisk, upright quarter-squat to load your quads and glutes.
Drive violently through the floor to extend your hips and knees, using that upward momentum to press the barbell straight overhead to lockout.
barbell-push-press.formTip: Keep your torso vertical during the dip—leaning forward pushes the bar out in front of you instead of straight overhead.

landmine-meadows-row.summary: Heavy single-arm landmine row (straddling the bar or perpendicular Meadows stance) for deep lat stretch and thick mid-back development.
steps: Stand staggered alongside or perpendicular to the loaded sleeve of the landmine barbell and hinge at the hips to a 45° flat-back angle.
Rest your non-working forearm on your front thigh and grip the barbell sleeve or collar with your working hand.
Drive your elbow back and high toward your hip crease, feeling a full lat and rhomboid contraction before lowering to a deep stretch.
landmine-meadows-row.formTip: Because the landmine pivots in an arc, pull your elbow slightly back toward your hip rather than straight vertical.

barbell-pendlay-row.summary: Heavy bilateral bent-over or Pendlay barbell row building thickness across the lats, rhomboids, traps, spinal erectors, and biceps.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart over the Olympic barbell, hinge your hips back until your torso is 15°–45° above parallel, and grip the bar just outside your knees.
Brace your core and pull the barbell explosively into your lower ribcage / upper abdomen by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top for a half-second, then lower the bar under control.
barbell-pendlay-row.formTip: Keep your hip hinge angle locked throughout the set—do not stand upright to heave the bar with momentum.

chest-supported-dumbbell-row.summary: Strict bilateral dumbbell row lying prone on a 30°–45° incline bench to eliminate lower-back momentum and isolate the lats, rhomboids, and rear delts.
steps: Set your bench to a 30°–45° incline and lie chest-down with your feet planted on the floor and dumbbells hanging straight down.
Retract your shoulder blades and drive both elbows back past your torso while keeping your chest glued to the pad.
Pause for 1 full second at peak back contraction, then lower the dumbbells slowly to a full dead-hang stretch.
chest-supported-dumbbell-row.formTip: Let your shoulder blades protract slightly at the bottom to stretch the lats, then initiate every pull by pinching the blades together.

high-band-lat-pulldown.summary: Straight-arm lat pulldown (prayer pulldown) using a large rubber band anchored to the pull-up bar to isolate the latissimus dorsi and serratus.
steps: Loop a medium-to-heavy rubber band over your pull-up bar, step back holding the band with both hands, and hinge forward 30°–45° with a flat back.
Keeping your arms straight (with only a soft 10° elbow lock), sweep your hands down in a wide arc from overhead all the way to your outer thighs.
Squeeze your lats and abs hard at the bottom for 1 second, then resist the band slowly as your arms return overhead.
high-band-lat-pulldown.formTip: Imagine pushing your hands down through heavy water—keep your shoulders depressed away from your ears so your lats do 100% of the work.

incline-dumbbell-curls.summary: Seated incline bench dumbbell curl placing the long head of the biceps under maximum loaded stretch behind the torso.
steps: Sit back against a 45°–60° incline bench holding dumbbells at arm’s length so your elbows hang slightly behind your torso.
Keeping your upper arms pinned perpendicular to the floor, curl the dumbbells up while supinating your wrists (palms up).
Squeeze your biceps at the top without letting your elbows drift forward, then lower slowly for 3 seconds to a full stretch.
incline-dumbbell-curls.formTip: Because the incline stretches the bicep tendon at the bottom, 20–35 lb dumbbells feel much heavier than standing curls—prioritize strict elbow position.

hammer-zottman-curls.summary: Dumbbell curl variation targeting the biceps, brachialis, and brachioradialis via neutral-grip hammer curls or eccentric-pronated Zottman curls.
steps: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides with a neutral "hammer" grip (palms facing each other) or supinated grip.
For Hammer Curls, curl straight up keeping thumbs pointed toward the ceiling; for Zottman Curls, curl up palms-up, then rotate palms-down at the top.
Lower the weights slowly over 2–3 seconds to full elbow extension while keeping your elbows glued to your ribs.
hammer-zottman-curls.formTip: Rotating to an overhand grip on the way down (Zottman style) builds massive forearm and elbow tendon resilience.

overhead-tricep-extension.summary: Seated or standing overhead dumbbell tricep extension stretching and overloading the long head of the triceps.
steps: Sit upright on a 90° bench (or flat bench) holding one heavy dumbbell vertically with both hands cupped under the top plate overhead.
Keep your elbows tucked in close to your ears and lower the dumbbell behind your head until your forearms reach a deep stretch below 90°.
Drive through your triceps to extend your arms straight back overhead without flaring your ribcage.
overhead-tricep-extension.formTip: Overhead shoulder flexion stretches the long head of the triceps—the largest muscle belly of the upper arm.

high-band-tricep-pushdown.summary: High-rep resistance band tricep pushdown anchored from the pull-up bar for joint-friendly lateral/medial tricep burnout.
steps: Loop a rubber band over your pull-up bar and grip both sides at chest height with your elbows pinned tightly against your ribs.
Without moving your upper arms, press the band straight down until your elbows are 100% locked out by your thighs.
Pull the ends of the band slightly apart at the bottom for a 1-second peak tricep contraction, then return to 90° elbow flexion.
high-band-tricep-pushdown.formTip: Keep your shoulders rolled back and down so your chest doesn’t hunch over the band.

landmine-180-rotations.summary: Explosive standing rotational rainbow sweep with the landmine barbell targeting the obliques, transverse abdominis, shoulders, and hips.
steps: Stand facing the landmine pivot with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the end of the barbell sleeve with both hands extended in front of you.
Sweep the barbell up in a high rainbow arc across the center line and lower it under control to your left hip while pivoting slightly on your back foot.
Brace your obliques to reverse the arc back overhead and down to your right hip in a smooth 180° rotational rhythm.
landmine-180-rotations.formTip: Keep your arms relatively long so your core and obliques control the rotational torque rather than turning it into a bicep curl.

hanging-leg-knee-raises.summary: Strict hanging knee or straight-leg raise from the pull-up bar to build lower rectus abdominis, oblique, hip flexor, and grip strength.
steps: Hang from your pull-up bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip, active shoulders (ears away from shoulders), and legs together.
Exhale and curl your pelvis upward (posterior pelvic tilt) to lift your knees—or straight legs—until your thighs pass parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top without swinging, then lower your legs slowly over 2–3 seconds back to a dead hang.
hanging-leg-knee-raises.formTip: Focus on curling your tailbone up toward the bar—if you only lift your knees to 90° with a flat pelvis, your hip flexors do all the work instead of your lower abs.

banded-pallof-press.summary: Anti-rotation isometric core press using a rubber band anchored to the squat rack upright tobulletproof the obliques and deep spinal stabilizers.
steps: Anchor a rubber band at chest height on your squat rack upright, stand sideways to the rack in an athletic stance, and hold the band at your sternum.
Step away until there is strong lateral tension trying to twist your torso toward the rack.
Press your hands straight out in front of your chest to full extension, hold for 2 seconds resisting all rotation, then return to your chest; switch sides halfway.
banded-pallof-press.formTip: Widen your stance for easier balance or narrow your feet together to make your obliques and glutes work twice as hard.

copenhagen-side-plank.summary: Side plank with the top foot/shin supported on a workout bench to intensely strengthen the inner-thigh adductors, obliques, and lateral hip stabilizers.
steps: Lie on your side perpendicular to your bench, prop yourself on your bottom forearm under your shoulder, and rest your top foot or shin on top of the bench.
Press your top leg down into the bench to lift your hips off the floor into a straight side plank line, hovering or lifting your bottom leg underneath.
Hold isometrically or perform controlled hip dips + adductor squeezes for half the interval before switching sides.
copenhagen-side-plank.formTip: Rest your inner knee/shin on the bench for a shorter lever if resting only your foot/ankle on the bench feels too intense on the groin.

pilates-hundred.summary: Signature Pilates mat endurance exercise holding a hollow curl with legs at 45° while pumping straight arms vigorously in 5-count breath cycles.
steps: Lie on your yoga mat, curl your head and shoulder blades up into a tight Pilates C-curve, and extend your legs out to a 45° angle (or tabletop).
Reach your arms long beside your hips 2 inches off the mat and pump them vigorously up and down 6–8 inches.
Inhale for 5 rapid arm pumps and exhale for 5 rapid arm pumps while keeping your lower back imprinted into the mat.
pilates-hundred.formTip: Look toward your navel and anchor your lower ribs down—if your neck fatigues, support your head with one hand while pumping the other.

pilates-single-double-leg-stretch.summary: Dynamic Pilates abdominal flow alternating single-leg knee pulls with full double-leg hollow extensions.
steps: Curl your head and shoulders off the yoga mat into an abdominal C-curve with knees drawn into tabletop.
Single-Leg Phase: Pull your right knee into your chest while extending your left leg long at 45°, switch legs for 2–4 reps.
Double-Leg Phase: Inhale to reach both arms overhead and both legs out to 45° simultaneously, then exhale to sweep your arms around and hug both knees in.
pilates-single-double-leg-stretch.formTip: Keep your shoulder blades lifted at the exact same height even when your arms and legs reach away from your center.

pilates-roll-up-teaser.summary: Articulated Pilates spinal roll-up transitioning smoothly into a balanced V-sit Teaser hold to develop deep core control and hamstring flexibility.
steps: Lie flat on your yoga mat with arms extended overhead and legs pressed tightly together.
Inhale to float your arms toward the ceiling, then exhale to peel your spine off the mat one vertebra at a time into a balanced V-sit Teaser with legs lifted at 45°.
Hold the Teaser balance for 1–2 seconds with arms parallel to your shins, then roll down slowly bone-by-bone to the mat.
pilates-roll-up-teaser.formTip: Avoid jerking with momentum through the sticking point—exhale deeply and hollow your navel back into your spine.

dead-bug-weighted-banded.summary: Contralateral anti-extension core exercise lying supine while extending opposite arm and leg under dumbbell or band tension.
steps: Lie on your back with knees in 90° tabletop, lower back pressed flat into the mat, and hands holding dumbbells (or a band anchored behind you) straight above your chest.
Slowly lower your right arm overhead and extend your left leg out to a 2-inch hover simultaneously without letting your lower back arch.
Exhale to return both limbs to the center tabletop position, then repeat with your left arm and right leg.
dead-bug-weighted-banded.formTip: Imagine crushing a grape under your lower back—if your lumbar spine lifts off the mat, shorten the leg extension slightly.

single-leg-trx-squats.summary: Unilateral single-leg TRX squat complex alternating 1 forward pistol squat (free leg in front) and 1 reverse shrimp squat (free leg behind) for 8 reps on one leg, then 8 on the other, holding lightly onto the TRX straps for balance.
steps: Stand facing the TRX anchor holding the handles lightly with fingertips at waist height—use the straps strictly for balance rather than pulling yourself up.

On your right standing leg, extend your left leg straight forward and descend into a deep Forward Single-Leg Squat, driving through your right heel to stand; immediately sweep your left leg back behind you and lower into a Reverse Single-Leg Squat.
Continue alternating Forward then Reverse squats until you complete 8 total reps on the right leg, then switch to complete 8 alternating Forward + Reverse reps on the left leg.
single-leg-trx-squats.formTip: Keep your grip feather-light on the TRX handles so your standing quad, glute, and hip stabilizers carry 95%+ of your bodyweight across both forward and reverse planes.

barbell-romanian-deadlift.summary: Heavy posterior-chain hip hinge with an Olympic barbell to overload the hamstrings, glutes, and spinal erectors through a deep eccentric stretch.
steps: Stand tall holding a loaded Olympic barbell against your upper thighs with a shoulder-width overhand grip and a soft 15° knee bend.
Push your hips straight back toward the wall behind you while keeping the barbell shaving close down your thighs and shins with a flat back.
Pause at mid-shin when you feel a maximal hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall.
barbell-romanian-deadlift.formTip: Keep your lats engaged as if squeezing oranges in your armpits so the barbell never drifts forward away from your shins.

barbell-deadlift.summary: Foundational full-body strength lift pulling a loaded Olympic barbell from the floor (conventional or sumo stance) to build total posterior-chain power.
steps: Stand with your mid-foot directly beneath the Olympic barbell (hip-width for Conventional or wide turnout for Sumo) and grip the bar outside or inside your knees.
Drop your hips until your shins touch the bar, lift your chest to flatten your back, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away with your legs while driving your hips forward to stand tall to full lockout, then return the bar to the floor under control.
barbell-deadlift.formTip: Think of the first half of the deadlift as a leg press through the floor, and the second half as a hip thrust once the bar passes your knees.

good-mornings-barbell-band.summary: Loaded hip hinge with an Olympic barbell across the upper back (or a thick rubber band looped under the feet and over the neck) targeting the hamstrings, glutes, and erectors.
steps: Place a barbell across your upper traps (or stand on a heavy loop band with the top looped behind your neck/shoulders) with feet shoulder-width apart.
Unlock your knees slightly and hinge your hips straight back until your torso is 15°–30° above parallel to the floor.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward powerfully to return to standing.
good-mornings-barbell-band.formTip: Brace your core 360° before every hinge so your lumbar spine remains rigid from start to finish.

nordic-bench-hamstring-bridge.summary: Long-lever feet-elevated hamstring bridge with heels dug into a workout bench to isolate the distal hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Lie on your back on the yoga mat and place both heels on top of your workout bench with your knees bent at roughly a 110°–120° long-lever angle.
Dig your heels straight down into the bench pad to lift your hips into a bridge without letting your lower back hyperextend.
Hold the intense hamstring contraction at the top for 1 full second (or perform single-leg eccentric lowers), then lower with control.
nordic-bench-hamstring-bridge.formTip: Keeping your knees slightly more extended (120° rather than 90°) shifts the load directly from the glutes onto the hamstrings.

barbell-hip-thrust.summary: Heavy bilateral glute builder with upper back supported on a bench and a loaded Olympic barbell across the hips (plus optional hip band above knees).
steps: Sit on the floor with your upper back/shoulder blades resting against the edge of your workout bench and roll a loaded barbell over your hip crease.
Plant your feet shoulder-width apart so your shins are vertical at the top, tuck your chin, and drive through your heels to lift the bar to full hip extension.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the flat tabletop lockout for 1–2 seconds, then lower your hips under control.
barbell-hip-thrust.formTip: Wear a hip band just above your knees while thrusting the barbell to simultaneously fire the upper/outer glute medius and glute maximus.

landmine-hack-goblet-squat.summary: Front-loaded squat holding the angled landmine barbell sleeve at the chest, allowing an upright torso that deeply targets the quads, glutes, and core.
steps: Stand facing the landmine holding the end of the loaded barbell sleeve cupped against your upper sternum with both hands and elbows tucked.
Lean slightly into the angled path of the bar as you sit your hips straight down into a deep full-range squat.
Drive through your mid-foot and heels to press back up along the bar’s arc to standing.
landmine-hack-goblet-squat.formTip: Because the landmine counterbalance lets you sit back without falling over, you can achieve deeper knee flexion and quad recruitment with zero lower-back strain.

landmine-lateral-cossack-lunge.summary: Frontal-plane lateral lunge (Cossack squat) loaded with the landmine or dumbbell to build outer glute, quad, and inner-thigh mobility and strength.
steps: Stand with a wide stance holding the landmine barbell sleeve (or a dumbbell) at chest or hip height.
Shift your weight laterally to the right, sitting your right hip back and down into a deep single-leg squat while keeping your left leg completely straight.
Drive forcefully through your right heel to return to the center, then repeat on the left side (or complete all reps on one side before switching).
landmine-lateral-cossack-lunge.formTip: Keep the heel of your working leg glued flat on the floor while letting the toes of your straight trail leg rotate upward if you sink into a deep Cossack squat.
